rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried vegetation; it may be pronounced with a light or doubled thāʾ.
rows.anchor: والغثاء : بضم الغين المعجمة وتخفيف المثلثة ، ويقال بتشديد المثلثة هو اليابس من النبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥwā describes a brown approaching black; dry plants turn this color as their green fades.
rows.anchor: الموصوف بالحُوَّة بضم الحاء وتشديد الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The color change from fresh green to dark dry growth evokes God's power to bring things into being and end them.
rows.anchor: لاستحضار تغيُّر لونه بعد أن كان أخضر يانعاً وذلك دليل على تصرفه تعالى بالإنشاء وبالإنهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pasture stands for Qur'anic guidance and law as rain-grown pasture benefits animals; the law likewise reaches its completion and full maturity.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى تمثيل حال القرآن وهدايته وما اشتمل عليه من الشريعة التي تنفع الناس بحال الغيث

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report compares the guidance and knowledge brought by the Prophet to abundant rain: receptive land grows abundant pasture, while land that retains water benefits people in other ways.
rows.anchor: بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « مثل ما بَعَثني الله به من الهُدى والعِلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may also teach that created things pass through opposite stages, recalling death after life and the brevity of worldly freshness.
rows.anchor: إدماج العبرة بتصاريف ما أودع الله في المخلوقات من مختلف الأطوار من الشيء إلى ضده للتذكير بالفناء بعد الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quick sequence marked by the particle in “then He made it dry” underscores how briefly the world's flourishing lasts, as in the parable of the harvested crop.
rows.anchor: الحرفُ الموضوع لعطف ما يحصل فيه حكم المعطوف بعدَ زمن قريب من زمن حصول المعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reassuring the Prophet about revelation and his mission, God commands him to continue proclaiming the Qur'an, strengthening his resolve and encouraging willing obedience.
rows.anchor: أعقب ذلك بأنْ أمَرَه بالتذكير ، أي التبليغ ، أي بالاستمرار عليه ، إرهافاً لعزمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed fa derives the command as the result of what preceded it; the imperative asks for continuing action, and reminder means conveying the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فالفاء للتفريع على ما تقدم تفريعَ النتيجة على المقدمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “remind” is omitted to make the command general, with the next verse identifying those who will remember.
rows.anchor: أي فذكر الناس ودلّ عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional phrase is parenthetical and does not limit the command: the Prophet is to remind everyone, since he cannot know in advance who will benefit.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة وليس متعلقاً بالجملة ولا تقييداً لمضمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call remains universal even though God knows who will accept guidance; Abu Jahl too is invited although God knows he will not believe.
rows.anchor: فالدعوة عامة وما يعلمه الله من أحوال الناس في قبول الهدى وعدمه أمر استأثر اللَّهُ بعلمه ، فأبو جهل مدعو للإِيمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the reminder benefits God's allies but not His enemies.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس : تنفع أوليائي ولا تنفع أعدائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using in rather than a definite condition hints that some people will not benefit, a point answered by the following statement that the God-fearing will remember.
rows.anchor: بأن في القوم من لا تنفعه الذكرى وذلك يفهم من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the need to supply al-Farrāʾ and al-Naḥḥās's “whether it benefits or does not,” since the one condition implies the other.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تقدير الفراء والنحاس : إن نفعت الذكرى وإن لم تنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhdhakkaru is the passive-response form of dhakkara; its original tāʾ assimilated to the following dhāl because their articulation points are close.
rows.anchor: ويذّكَّر : مُطاوع ذَكَّره . وأصله : يتذكر ، فقلبت التاء ذالاً لقرب مخرجيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun for fatness means an animal's abundance of flesh and fat; food is said to make it fat when it produces that condition.
rows.anchor: والسِمن ، بكسر السين وفتح الميم : وفرة اللحم والشحم للحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ighnāʾ means sufficing or meeting a need; min with hunger marks substitution, meaning the food cannot replace hunger with nourishment.
rows.anchor: أي غناء بدلاً عن الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restricted food statements in this verse and 69:36 support identifying ḍarīʿ as a tree of Hell from which ghislin flows.
rows.anchor: أن الضريع اسم شجر جهنم يسيل منه الغسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this sentence could have been coordinated with the description of downcast faces, it is separated to answer the implied question whether the Hereafter has a joyful scene too.
rows.anchor: فجاءت الجملة بعدها مفصولة لأنها جعلت استئنافاً بيانياً جواباً عن سؤال مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent sentence works as an aside and completion, displaying the contrast between the two groups and following warning with glad tidings, a Qur'anic pattern of alternating threat and encouragement.
rows.anchor: لإظهار الفرق بين حالي الفريقين ولتعقيب النذارة بالبشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first faces belong to those who denied the Messenger, while the later faces belong to believers who affirmed his message.
rows.anchor: الوجوه الأولى وجوه المكذبين بالرسول ، والوجوه المذكورة بعدها وجوه المؤمنين المصدقين بما جاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāʿimah may derive from softness and a pleasant appearance, or from having a life of blessing, comfort, and luxury.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مشتقاً من نُعم بضم العين ينعُمُ بضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāʿimah is the predicate of wujūh; its interpretation and the indefinite use of faces follow the preceding verses' pattern.
rows.anchor: الذي مصدره نعومة وهي اللين وبهجة المرأى وحسن المنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarābī is the plural of zarbiyyah, a soft, colored woolen carpet or rug spread for sitting and decoration among the wealthy.
rows.anchor: المنسوج من الصوف الملون الناعم يفرش في الأرض للزينة والجلوس عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarbiyyah is traced to a nisbah from Azerbaijān: its initial hamzah was dropped for ease, and the Persian place-name's z was represented in Arabic with dhāl.
rows.anchor: فأصل زربية أذربية ، حذفت همزتها للتخفيف لثقل الاسم لعجمته واتصال ياء النسب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azerbaijān was known for fine sheep's wool and for the fine weave and soft pile of its rugs.
rows.anchor: واشتهر أيضاً بدقة صنع البُسُط والطنافس ورقّة خَمَلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rugs are scattered widely over the ground; their being spread in abundance is implicit in the description.
rows.anchor: والمبثوثة : المنتشرة على الأرض بكثرة وذلك يفيد كناية عن الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The furnishings of Paradise answer the traits of Hell: comfortable, agreeable faces and activity are set against the dismay and hardship of the condemned.
rows.anchor: أهل النار بصفات وجوه أهل الجنة فقوبلت صفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The running spring, abundant drink, and luxurious resting places contrast with Hell's boiling water and starvation.
rows.anchor: وقوبل شقاء عيش أهل النار الذي أفاده قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are promised in Paradise what they recognize as delight, summarized as whatever souls desire and eyes enjoy, though its luxury exceeds verbal description.
rows.anchor: وهذا وعد للمؤمنين بأن لهم في الجنة ما يعرفون من النعيم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report adds delights no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.
rows.anchor: ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa branches from the surah's account of the Resurrection and their rejection into an order to keep reminding them, despite their refusal to listen.
rows.anchor: رتب على ذلك أمر الله رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالدوام على تذكيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuing command reassures the Prophet that he bears no blame when they fail to listen; he was not sent to compel belief.
rows.anchor: وتثبيته بأنه لا تبعة عليه من عدم إصغائهم إذ لم يُبعث مُلجئاً لهم على الإِيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “remind” is omitted and supplied by the later phrase that he is not their controller; the imperative asks for continued effort.
rows.anchor: بالدوام على تذكيرهم وأنه لا يؤيسه إصرارهم على الإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innamā gives an additional restriction: the Messenger's role is reminder, not an agent responsible for producing their recollection, so their failure does not make him negligent.
rows.anchor: لست وكيلاً على تحصيل تذكرهم فلا تتحرج من عدم تذكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is not itself the oath's answer: it either evidences an unstated threat of destruction or introduces the later answer that God watches the deniers.
rows.anchor: لا يصلح هذا أن يكون جواباً للقسم ولكنه : إمَّا دليلُ الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the answer is that God watches the deniers, the intervening history builds anticipation and prepares the mind to accept the threat.
rows.anchor: وإمّا تمهيد للجواب ومقدمة له إن جعلت الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is confirmatory and addressed to the Prophet for reassurance and a promise of victory, while warning opponents through the fate of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: تقريري ، والمخاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تثبيتاً له ووعداً بالنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recalling comparable destructions makes a rare event mentally vivid and removes the audience's tendency to dismiss its recurrence.
rows.anchor: لأن بُعد العهد بحدوث أمثاله ينسيه الناسَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾayta may denote certain knowledge, likened to clear sight because the communities' stories were famous, or literal sight of their traces.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون رؤية عِلْمية تشبيهاً للعلم اليقيني بالرؤية في الوضوح والانكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With knowledge-based seeing, kayfa is an interrogative that suspends the verb from taking its two objects; with visual seeing, it is a noun in the object position.
rows.anchor: استفهاماً معلِّقاً فعل الرؤية عن العمل في مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “your Lord” evokes care, support, honor, and the Prophet's special standing.
rows.anchor: لِما في وصف رب من الإِشعار بالولاية والتأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd and Thamūd are named first because they were familiar to the audience; Pharaoh follows because Moses' mission was known among Arabian Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: وقد ابتُدئت الموعظة بذكر عاد وثمود لشهرتهما بين المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd means the tribe; Īram is its ancestral tribe-name, referring to Īram son of Sām and ancestor through ʿAws, and the name is treated as foreign and indeclinable.
rows.anchor: وهو ممنوع من الصرف للعجمة لأن العرب البائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine description applies to ʿĀd because the referent is a tribe; ʿimād is literally a thick, tall support for a house or tent.
rows.anchor: وصْف مؤنث لأن المراد بعاد القبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pillar is a metaphor for strength, comparing the powerful tribe to a sturdy tent or house supported by pillars.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا مستعار للقوة تشبيهاً للقبيلة القوية بالبيت ذات العماد

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's verse uses ʿimād for a clan's strength and protection of those around it.
rows.anchor: في قول عمرو بن كلثوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the pillars as markers built along roads to guide travelers, like the structures mentioned in 26:128.
rows.anchor: الأعلام التي بنوْها في طرُقهم ليهتدي بها المسافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description stresses that God destroyed a people stronger than the Prophet's opponents, as also stated in 47:13 and 40:21.
rows.anchor: أي قد أهلك الله قوماً هم أشد من القوم الذين كذبوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine relative pronoun refers to ʿĀd understood as a tribe; Arabic likewise uses feminine tribal names for their peoples.
rows.anchor: تَغلِبُ ابنةُ وائل ، بتأويل تغلب بالقبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilād is the plural of balad or baldah, a broad, bounded or inhabited region; the definite article can refer generically to the earth.
rows.anchor: وهي مساحة واسعة من الأرض معيَّنة بحدود أو سكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness denied is likeness to that people on earth; the stronger contextual sense of al-bilād is the lands and tribes of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وأريد بالخلق خلق أجسادهم فقد رُوي أنهم كانوا طِوالاً شداداً أقوياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe the people as tall, strong, intelligent, and prudent; Arabs proverbialized their judgment, though luxury later corrupted their character.
rows.anchor: وكانوا أهل عقل وتدبير ، والعرب تضرب المثل بأحلام عاد ، ثم فسدت طباعهم بالترف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article most likely denotes the familiar scope of Arab lands and tribes rather than every land without exception.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن لام التعريف هنا للاستغراق العُرفي ، أي في بلدان العرب وقبائلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the storytellers' fabricated city of Īram and the tale of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qilābah finding it under Muʿāwiyah.
rows.anchor: وقد وضع القصاصون حول قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city story fails grammatically: a compound name would put both parts in the accusative, while a singular name qualified by dhāt gives no reason for its genitive.
rows.anchor: فلو كان الاسم مركباً مَزْجياً لكان بناء جزأيْه على الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city interpretation also conflicts with Īram's placement directly after the words “with ʿĀd.”
rows.anchor: على أن موقع هذا الاسم عقب قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about those who transgress may describe all three peoples or specifically Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون شاملاً لجميع المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون . ويجوز أن يكون نعتاً لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān means extreme disobedience and injustice; each people transgressed in its own land, and local oppression spreads through the lands.
rows.anchor: والطغيان شدّة العصيان والظلم ومعنى طغيانهم في البلاد أن كل أمة من هؤلاء طغوا في بلدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tyranny multiplies corruption by teaching others to violate rights; it also breeds hatred and fear, divides society, and weakens its ability to face external enemies.
rows.anchor: فلا جرم كان الطغيان سبباً لكثرة الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bilād may use a familiar referent for the lands of those peoples, with the plural distributed so each nation is assigned its own land.
rows.anchor: أي في بلادهم والجمع على اعتبار التوزيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamm means plentiful; describing love, an abstract emotion, as plentiful is a metaphor for intense, excessive love.
rows.anchor: فالجمّ مستعار لمعنى القوي الشديد ، أي حبّاً مفرطاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excessive attachment to wealth is blameworthy because it drives people to acquire it through wrongful means such as seizure, embezzlement, theft, and betrayal of trusts.
rows.anchor: لأن إفراد حبه يوقع في الحِرص على اكتسابه بالوسائل غير الحَق كالغصب والاختلاس والسرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the preceding failures to honor orphans, encourage feeding the poor, respect inheritance, and restrain excessive love of wealth.
rows.anchor: زجر وردع عن الأعمال المعدودة قبله ، وهي عدم إكرامهم اليتيم وعدم حضهم على طعام المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from the threatened worldly fate of earlier peoples to the unavoidable punishment of the Hereafter, when remembrance comes too late.
rows.anchor: انتقل به من تهديدهم بعذاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apocalyptic details before the warning's central statements set the scene, build suspense, and magnify that Day's terror.
rows.anchor: فهو توطئة وتشويق لسماع ما يجيء بعده وتهويل لشأن ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakk means crushing or breaking; the earth is the inhabited globe, whose parts are shattered through the breakdown of its present order, as in the earthquake passage.
rows.anchor: والدّك : الحَطْم والكسر . والمراد بالأرض الكُرَة التي عليها الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes the first dakkā an emphatic direct object securing literal, actual crushing, and the second a verbal repetition that further confirms it; unusual destruction warrants this emphasis.
rows.anchor: الأول مقصود به رفع احتمال المجاز عن

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī allows a verbal repetition to emphasize an indefinite noun when it is a predicate rather than a subject, citing the repeated declaration that a marriage is invalid.
rows.anchor: درج الرضي قال : ويستثنى من منع تأكيد النكرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following al-Kashshāf and most exegetes, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers reading the two maṣdars together as successive, detailed blows; this adds a sense of unfolding detail beyond emphasis.
rows.anchor: أنه دكّ يعقُب بعضه بعضاً كما تقول

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf and most later exegetes explain the repeated noun as a kind of crushing that follows repeatedly, like reading a book chapter by chapter.
rows.anchor: فسّر صاحب « الكشاف » وجمهور المفسرين من بعده

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Fakhr's interpretation, followed by al-Bayḍāwī, takes the crushing as flattening the earth and mountains into a level plain.
rows.anchor: في « تفسير الفخر » : وقيل : فبُسِطَتَا بسطةً واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further figurative reading treats the doubled form as one uniquely severe blow, but Ibn ʿĀshūr finds that strained because the corresponding singular adjective is unattested.
rows.anchor: ولك أن تجعل صفة واحدة مجازاً في تفرد الدكة بالشدة التي لا ثاني مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is called Sūrat Lā Uqsim in al-Bukhārī's chapter heading and Sūrat al-Balad in Qur'an copies and tafsir works.
rows.anchor: وسميت في المصاحف وكتب التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr holds the surah Meccan: most exegetes and al-Zamakhsharī and al-Qurṭubī report agreement, though Ibn ʿAṭiyyah cites a Medinan view.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية وحكى الزمخشري والقرطبي الاتفاق عليه واقتصر عليه معظم المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Medinan dating was linked to interpreting “you are lawful in this city” as permission to fight there on the day of the conquest.
rows.anchor: أن الحل الإذن له في القتال يوم الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says al-Zamakhsharī's appeal to consensus begs the question; the pronouns later in the surah instead have an antecedent in “the human” and support its Meccan setting.
rows.anchor: فالوجه أن يورد بأن في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Itqān records another view that the surah is Medinan except for its first four verses.
rows.anchor: وحكى في الإتقان قولا أنها مدنية إلا الآيات الأربع من أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is the thirty-fifth surah in revelation order, after Qāf and before al-Ṭāriq, and has twenty verses.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت الخامسة والثلاثين في عدد نزول السور ، نزلت بعد سورة ق وقبل سورة الطارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its purposes include honoring Mecca, the Prophet's place and blessing there, and his ancestors among its prophets and adherents of the primordial faith.
rows.anchor: حوت من الأغراض التنويه بمكة . وبمقام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بها . وبركته فيها وعلى أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It rebukes polytheist conduct, denial of resurrection, boastfulness, ingratitude for perception, speech, thought, and guidance, and neglect of faith and generosity; it warns disbelievers and gives believers good news.
rows.anchor: والتخلص إلى ذم سيرة أهل الشرك . وإنكارهم البعث . وما كانوا عليه من التفاخر المبالغ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā uqsim means “I swear”; interpreters differ whether lā is redundant negation or retains its force as an allusion to the greatness of the object.
rows.anchor: هل حرف النفي مزيد أو هو مستعمل في معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This points to Mecca, constantly present in the hearers' experience; the demonstrative marks it out distinctly and honors it.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حاضر في أذهان السامعين كأنهم يرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balad means an expanse of land, inhabited or empty; here it is the built-up settlement of Mecca, and swearing by it alludes to God's honoring it.
rows.anchor: وأطلق هنا على جانب من الأرض مجعولة فيه بيوت من بناء وهو بلدة مكة

rows.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
rows.claim: Ruʾbah ibn al-ʿAjjāj's line uses balad for a broad expanse across whose ravines darkness stretches.
rows.anchor: رؤبة بن العجاج : بلْ بَلَدٍ ملءُ الفجاج قَتمُه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question explains the rebuke of people who think no one can overpower or see them: God created perception and speech, so the giver of knowledge cannot be powerless or ignorant.
rows.anchor: أي هو غافل عن قدرة الله تعالى وعن علمه المحيط بجميع الكائنات الدال عليهما أنه خَلَق مشاعر الإِدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may be confirmatory or reproachful.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام يجوز أن يكون تقريرياً وأن يكون إنكارياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes are singled out because they are the most useful sense and because the immediate point challenges the assumption that no one sees the person.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار على العينين لأنهما أنفع المشاعر ولأن المعلَّل إنكار ظنه إن لم يره أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lips are named with the tongue because articulation requires them together; neither can speak without the other.
rows.anchor: وذِكْر الشفتين مع اللسان لأن الإِبانة تحصل بهما معاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By naming both organs, the Qur'an gives a more exact depiction than Arab idioms that mention only a tongue or only a lip, fitting the verse's argument from creation.
rows.anchor: ومن دقائق القرآن أنه لم يقتصر على اللسان ولا على الشفتين خلاف عادة كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of moral guidance follows perception and speech, completing the foundations of learning and teaching: sensing acquires knowledge, speech shares it, and guidance tests it.
rows.anchor: فاستكمل الكلامُ أصول التعلُّم والتعليم فإن الإِنسان خُلق محباً للمعرفة محباً للتعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lips cover the mouth and teeth, help draw in water, and shape speech sounds by opening and closing.
rows.anchor: والشفتان هما الجِلدتان اللتان تستران الفم وأسنانه وبهما يُمتص الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation gives shafah an original wāw, removed and replaced by tāʾ marbūṭah; another treats hāʾ as the original final consonant.
rows.anchor: وأصل شفة شَفَو نقص منه الواو وعوض عنه هاء فيجمع على شفوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr favors original hāʾ: it was treated like feminine tāʾ for ease in connected speech and in the dual, as required when a noun returns to its root in dual formation.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الأصل شفه بهاء أصلية ثم عوملت الهاء معاملة هاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miskīn means a poor person; “of dust” is a customary sign of extreme need, suggesting someone without bedding who lies on the ground.
rows.anchor: صفة لمسكين جعلت المتربة علامة على الاحتياج بحسب العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mat­raba comes from tariba, to lie on soil without a bed; by extension it suggests having no clothes to separate one's body from the ground, like the expressions wishing dust upon someone's hand.
rows.anchor: وهو في الأصل كناية عن العُروِّ من الثياب التي تحول بين الجسد والأرض عند الجلوس والاضطجاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw divides into alternatives and also conveys choice.
rows.anchor: للتقسيم وهو معنى من معاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “the human” means the polytheists collectively, their failure to free captives or feed the needy signals rejection of Islamic practices and rebukes their showy, self-serving banquets.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه إن كان المراد بالإنسان الجنس المخصوص ، أي المشركين كان نفي فكّ الرقاب والإِطعام كنايةً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meal God approves relieves needy people on a day of hunger; elite banquets instead invited the well-off for company and prestige.
rows.anchor: أي هو الطعام الذي يرضاه الله لأن فيه نفع المحتاجين من عباده . وليس مثل إطعامكم في المآدب والولائم

rows.speaker: مسلم
rows.claim: A report in Muslim calls a wedding banquet the worst food because it excludes those who come and invites those who refuse.
rows.anchor: حديث مسلم " شر الطعام طعامُ الوليمة يُمْنَعْها

rows.speaker: الطبراني
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports a variant: the banquet invites the satiated and withholds food from the hungry.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبراني : " شرّ الطعام طعام الوليمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse concerns a particular person, it may similarly condemn miserliness and false boasting, exposing that he had done no prior good for his people by ransoming captives or freeing slaves.
rows.anchor: وجاز أن يكون ذَمّاً له باللّؤْم والتفاخرِ الكاذب ، وفضحاً له بأنه لم يسبق منه عمل نافع لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish that God charged polytheists with these good works or punished them for neglecting them, so the debate over whether unbelievers are addressed by legal duties is misplaced here.
rows.anchor: فليس في الآية دلالة على أن الله كلف المشركين بهذه القرب ولا أنه عاقبهم على تركهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may answer the oath, promising the believers' success and the polytheists' failure, as the oath response does in al-Layl.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الجملة جواب القسم ، وإن المعنى تحقيق فلاح المؤمنين وخَيبة المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may interrupt the oath before its answer, linking God's inspiration of vice and piety to the success of one who purifies the soul and follows piety.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملةً معترضة بين القَسم والجواب لمناسبة ذكر إلهام الفجور والتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This prepares for the account of Thamūd: their punishment exemplifies the failure of those who pollute themselves with transgression.
rows.anchor: فإن ما أصاب ثمودا كان من خيبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success comes first to match piety; failure follows to prepare the transition to Thamūd's punishment for moral corruption.
rows.anchor: وقدم الفلاح على الخيبة لمناسبته للتقوى ، وأردف بخيبة من دسى نفسه لتهيئة الانتقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who purifies is the human being, with the self and person treated as two things because of intention and acquired action.
rows.anchor: الإِنسان والنفس شيء واحد ، ونزلا منزلة شيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiyah means increasing goodness.
rows.anchor: والتزكية : الزيادة من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dassa-hā means keeping the soul from doing good; the root means hiding something by putting it under something else.
rows.anchor: حال بينها وبين فعل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled consonant in dassā was changed to yāʾ for ease, as in the forms taqaḍḍā/taqaḍḍaḍ and tazannaytu.
rows.anchor: فأبدلوا الحرف المضاعف ياء طلباً للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If purification answers the oath, the account of Thamūd demonstrates the failure expressed here.
rows.anchor: في موقع الدليل لمضمون جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People seek either lasting benefit and perfection or immediate, false gains that decay into loss; this verse describes the latter as failure in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: والمقصود هنا الفلاح في الآخرة والخيبة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage repeatedly uses antithesis: sun/moon, day/night, illumination/covering, heaven/earth, building/spreading, vice/piety, success/failure, and purification/corruption.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات مُحسّن الطباق غير مرّة فقد ذكرت أشياء متقابلة متضادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh marks the time attached to Thamūd's transgression: when the most wretched rose to hamstring the she-camel, their extreme defiance became manifest.
rows.anchor: لأن وقت انبعاث أشقاها لعقر الناقة هو الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people sent their most wretched man to kill the she-camel God had given them as a sign, reaching the height of audacity.
rows.anchor: التي جُعلت لهم آية وذلك منتهى الجُرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inbaʿatha is the responsive form of baʿatha: they sent him, and he rose and volunteered for the task.
rows.anchor: بعثوا أشقاهم فانبعث وانتدب لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a verbal noun marker; the oath invokes the creation of male and female as an effect of divine power and the reproduction that follows.
rows.anchor: مصدرية أقسم الله بأثر من آثار قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female refer to animal kinds, with particular focus on human creation because humans are the highest material beings and repeatedly observe their own formation.
rows.anchor: والمراد : خصوص خلق الإنسان وتكونه من ذكر وأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wonder is that the sexes differ though they arise from one origin, and reproduction depends on their joining.
rows.anchor: من اختلاف حالي الذكورة والأنوثة مع خروجهما من أصل واحد ، وتوقف التناسل على تزاوجهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theologians agree that divine acts are affirmed but differ over whether action attributes are eternal, as al-Māturīdī holds, or temporal as relations of power, as al-Ashʿarī holds; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this ultimately verbal.
rows.anchor: فهي موصوفة بالقدم عند الماتريدي ، أو جَعْلِها من تعلق صفة القدرة فهي حادثة عند الأشعري ، وهو آيل إلى الخلاف اللفظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the oath in al-Shams about the soul's creation of reason and knowledge, this oath concerns the body and sex differentiation; the response is the diversity of human striving.
rows.anchor: وقد كان القسم في سورة الشمس بتسوية النفس ، أي خلق العقل والمعرفة في الإِنسان ، وأما القَسَم هنا فبِخلق جسد الإِنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's emphasis supports the warning that wealth will not avail a person when he falls into ruin.
rows.anchor: من التأكيد بالقسم قولُه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy literally means vigorous, brisk walking, and is figuratively used for work and effort.
rows.anchor: والسَّعي حقيقته : المشي القوي الحثيث ، وهو مستعار هنا للعمل والكدّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shattā is a broken plural meaning widely differing; it metaphorically or implicitly describes diverse deeds, as dispersion entails difference.
rows.anchor: وأريد به هنا التنوع والاختلاف في الأحوال كما في قول تأبط شرّاً

rows.speaker: تأبط شرّاً
rows.claim: The poet Taʾabbaṭa Sharran's phrase shattā al-nawā wa-l-masālik witnesses the word's sense of divergent paths and aims.
rows.anchor: كما في قول تأبط شرّاً : قليل التشكي للملم يصيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This resumes verses 5–10 and assigns responsibility to those choosing wrongdoing: God has excused them by directing them toward good, while each inclination brings facilitation toward its corresponding path.
rows.anchor: استئناف مقرّر لمضمون الكلام السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inclination underlying choice is called acquisition by al-Ashʿarī, the servant's capacity by the Muʿtazilites, and compulsion by the determinists.
rows.anchor: المعبَّرُ عنه بالكسب عند الأشعري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic inna and lām answer the thought that, if God wanted people to believe, He would compel them; the same objection is quoted elsewhere.
rows.anchor: يومىء إلى أن هذا كالجواب عما يجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā conveys obligation: God undertakes guidance as an act of grace and wisdom before holding people accountable.
rows.anchor: أي لازم لنا هُدَى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first created humans able to distinguish right and wrong, then sent messengers to clarify ambiguous matters and remind them of harms they may overlook.
rows.anchor: فهدى الله الإنسان بأن خلقه قابلاً للتمييز بين الصلاح والفساد ثم عزز ذلك بأن أرسل إليه رُسُلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “I warned you” is past tense in its literal sense, fa introduces a detailed warning from the previous general warning, much like an explanatory fa.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الفاء لمجرد التفريع الذِكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the past form can describe a present warning, drawing past time close to the present; then the warning follows from God's undertaking to guide.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للتفريع المعنوي فيكون فعلُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun “fire” magnifies its terror, and telazzā describes its intense blazing.
rows.anchor: وتلظى : تلتهب من شدة الاشتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb comes from laẓiyat al-nār, “the fire blazed”; its original form tatalaẓẓā lost one of the two tāʾs for brevity.
rows.anchor: تتلظى بتاءين حذفت إحداهما للاختصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second iqraʾ repeats the first to emphasize the command.
rows.anchor: تأكيد ل { اقرأ } الأول للاهتمام بهذا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence “your Lord is the Most Generous” begins an explanatory answer to how the Prophet can read when he lacks literacy; the One who taught by the pen can teach him.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أن الذي علّم الناس الكتابة بالقلم والقراءة قادر على أن يعلمك القراءة وأنت لا تعلم الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read alongside ʿĀʾishah's revelation report and Gabriel's repeated command, the sentence answers the Prophet's “I cannot read”: knowledge can come through dictation, instruction, or inspiration.
rows.anchor: عن قوله لجبريل : « ما أنا بقارىء » فالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught Adam the names even though Adam was not a reader, illustrating knowledge imparted without literacy.
rows.anchor: وقد علم الله آدم الأسماء ولم يكن آدم قارئاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected pronoun is replaced by rabbuka to emphasize divine care and to keep the Lord-title connected to the command to read in His name.
rows.anchor: لتأكيد ما يشعر به { ربّك } من العناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-akram intensifies generosity rather than comparing God with others; karam is giving the recipient beneficial gifts, including existence, creation, and sustenance.
rows.anchor: مصوغ للدلالة على قوة الاتصاف بالكرم وليس مصوغاً للمفاضلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: Lordship entails existence and oneness; creation and teaching entail action; the Most Generous conveys perfection and freedom from defect.
rows.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two objects of “taught by the pen” are omitted and understood as teaching writers or people how to write.
rows.anchor: محذوفان دل عليهما قوله : { بالقلم } وتقديره : علّم الكاتبين

rows.speaker: أبو حية النميري
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyah al-Numayrī's verse uses a Jew's hand writing as evidence for the association of writing with the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حية النُّميري : كما خُطّ الكتابُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says writing first appeared among Arabs in al-Anbār; Ḥarb ibn Umayyah brought it to the Ḥijāz from Aslam ibn Sidrah, who learned it from Murāmir ibn Murrah; Ḥimyar had an earlier script called Musnad.
rows.anchor: وذُكر أن ظهور الخط في العرب أول ما كان عند أهل الأنبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause is placed between subject and predicate to answer the Prophet's fear that he could not read because he could not write: God can teach him reading.
rows.anchor: اعتذار عن تعذر امتثال أمره بقوله : { اقرأ } ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another hypothetical intensifies the wonder: would the opponent forbid a servant firmly guided, or one who commands piety? Since he forbids prayer, he forbids guidance and may also forbid counsel to piety.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : أرأيته إن كان العبد على الهدى أينهاه عن الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer is omitted and inferred as “would he forbid him too”; in answers, in leaves the condition's occurrence uncertain to match the scenario.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف وأتى بحرف الشرط الذي الغالب فيه عدم الجزم بوقوع فعل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾayta is cognitive, with its two objects omitted; ʿalā expresses figurative elevation, the servant's firm establishment in guidance, as in Luqmān.
rows.anchor: للاستعلاء المجازي وهو شدّة التمكن من الهُدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden subjects of kāna and amara refer to the servant, even though nearby pronouns refer to the forbidding person; context resolves each pronoun's antecedent.
rows.anchor: عائدان إلى { عبداً } وإن كانت الضمائر الحافّة به عائدة إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse illustrates that pronouns can refer to different antecedents according to context.
rows.anchor: قول عباس بن مرداس : عُدنا ولولا نَحْنُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of raʾayta is understood from the prior “forbids” or from the following reminder that God sees; the repeated hypothetical is separated because it renews the wonder about one person.
rows.anchor: لوقوعها موقع التكرير لأن فيها تكرير التَّعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another hypothetical intensifies the wonder: would the opponent forbid a servant firmly guided, or one who commands piety? Since he forbids prayer, he forbids guidance and may also forbid counsel to piety.
rows.anchor: أو إن كان العبد آمراً بالتقوى أينهاه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer is omitted and inferred as “would he forbid him too”; in answers, in leaves the condition's occurrence uncertain to match the scenario.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف وأتى بحرف الشرط الذي الغالب فيه عدم الجزم بوقوع فعل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾayta is cognitive, with its two objects omitted; ʿalā expresses figurative elevation, the servant's firm establishment in guidance, as in Luqmān.
rows.anchor: للاستعلاء المجازي وهو شدّة التمكن من الهُدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden subjects of kāna and amara refer to the servant, even though nearby pronouns refer to the forbidding person; context resolves each pronoun's antecedent.
rows.anchor: عائدان إلى { عبداً } وإن كانت الضمائر الحافّة به عائدة إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse illustrates that pronouns can refer to different antecedents according to context.
rows.anchor: قول عباس بن مرداس : عُدنا ولولا نَحْنُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of raʾayta is understood from the prior “forbids” or from the following reminder that God sees; the repeated hypothetical is separated because it renews the wonder about one person.
rows.anchor: لوقوعها موقع التكرير لأن فيها تكرير التَّعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fresh threat asks whether the person who denies and turns away supposes God is unaware of him; the first object of raʾayta is an omitted pronoun referring to the forbidding person.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة للتهديد والوعيد على التكذيب والتولي

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf takes “does he not know that God sees?” as the conditional answer, without the fa usually required before an interrogative answer.
rows.anchor: هو { ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } كذا قدر صاحب « الكشاف »

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī explicitly permits an interrogative conditional answer without fa, citing a parallel question in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: وصرح الرضي باختيار عدم اشتراط الاقتران بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians, including al-Zamakhsharī in al-Mufaṣṣal, require the answer to be joined by fa.
rows.anchor: جمهور النحاة والزمخشري في « المفصَّل » فهو وجوب الاقتران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later kallā is the proper point of rebuke, reinforcing the earlier one that was moved forward to create suspense.
rows.anchor: أكّد الردع الأول بحرف الردع الثاني في آخر الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning follows the rebuke: if the opponent does not stop, God will seize him by the forelock.
rows.anchor: أعقب الردع بالوعيد على فعله إذا لم يرتدع وينته عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām introduces an oath and the emphatic verb answers it; the conditional answer is omitted because the oath's answer supplies it.
rows.anchor: واللام موطئة للقسم ، وجملة « لنسفَعَنْ » جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ is a forceful grasp and pull; the forelock is the hair at the front of the head, and seizing it means dragging someone helplessly to punishment, with humiliation.
rows.anchor: والسفْع : القبض الشديد بجَذْب . والناصية مقدَّم شعر الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added bāʾ on the object intensifies the sense of firm attachment in the seizure.
rows.anchor: وأكدَ ذلك السفع بالباء المزيدة الداخلة على المفعول لتأكيد اللصوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the light emphatic nūn, common in affirmative oaths; the written alif reflects its pronunciation at pause, where final letters are often written as pronounced in pausal form.
rows.anchor: والنون نون التوكيد الخفيفة التي يكثر دخولها في القسم المثبَت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the forelock” is anticipatory and means “his forelock,” referring to the person who forbids prayer.
rows.anchor: للعهد التقديري ، أي بناصيته ، أي ناصية الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan grammarians call this article a substitute for a genitive possessor, a fitting name; Basrans reject that label and posit an omitted complement instead.
rows.anchor: وهذه اللام هي التي يسميها نحاة الكوفة عوضاً عن المضاف إليه . وهي تسمية حسنة وإن أباها البصريون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāṣiyah is an appositive to the forelock, made indefinite to refer to the class: a forelock of the lying, erring kind.
rows.anchor: بدل من الناصية وتنكيرها لاعتبار الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾah is the active participle of khaṭiʾa, to commit a sin; calling the forelock a liar and sinner is a rational metaphor for its owner.
rows.anchor: ووصفُ الناصية بالكاذبة والخاطئة مجاز عقلي . والمراد : كاذب صاحبُها خاطِىء صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The personification imagines the owner's lies and sins visibly emerging from his forehead, making the forelock fit for seizure.
rows.anchor: أنّ فيه تخييلاً بأن الكذب والخِطءَ بَاديان من ناصيته فكانت الناصية جديرة بالسفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyimah means upright and sound: uprightness metaphorically conveys perfection and correctness, like something standing ready for beneficial work; its opposite is crookedness.
rows.anchor: والقيِّمة : المستقيمة ، أي شديدة القيام الذي هو هنا مجاز في الكمال والصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form of the adjective treats the described collective as a group.
rows.anchor: وتأنيث الوصف لاعتبار كونه وصفاً لجمع
